Peter,
Recently, MSNBC’s _Morning Joe_ aired a powerful critique of the legacy media’s pro-Trump bias. Host Joe Scarborough called out major outlets like _The New York Times_ and _The Wall Street Journal_ for scrutinizing Kamala Harris' qualifications while giving Donald Trump a pass on his mental fitness and divisive, hate-driven campaign.
[**We’ll explain why we agree in a moment, but if you support COURIER’s work to expose media bias in the final days of the election, can you chip in $25 now?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95381109/506533073/-593472309?refcode=20241019-EM-MorningJoe&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzI0ODQ3Y2ItM2I4ZS1lZjExLTg0NzQtMDAwZDNhOThmYTZiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=xb1K0gIhQ8ne0wLEYJdMVonc07vZunNrxzpvmwuedd4=)
For a decade, Trump’s rise to power has been closely tied to the legacy media’s obsession with "both sides" reporting.
Rather than discussing policy or trying to unify the country, Trump thrives by dividing the public, spreading hate and conspiracy theories.
**Like many authoritarians, he creates chaos and then claims he’s the only one who can fix it.**
In 2024, Trump’s rhetoric has become even darker. His speeches increasingly include calls to violence, and he often sounds incoherent, revealing a sharp decline in his mental faculties.
**For these reasons and more, Trump is not fit for public office. As General Mark Milley, who served under Trump, warned, Trump is “fascist to the core” and “the most dangerous man in this country.”**
Yet, because of the “both sides” logic, media outlets that report these truths are accused of bias. This allows Trump’s fascist behavior to go unchecked by the press, and voters don’t get a sense of the real danger he poses to our democracy.
Take this week’s _Fox News_ interview with Bret Baier and Kamala Harris. Baier spent much of the interview grilling Harris, pushing right-wing talking points, and cutting her off. At one point, he even aired a Trump campaign ad, amplifying Trump’s message further to the 8 million watching at home.
**So why did Baier—once seen as a serious journalist—fall into this trap? As Scarborough pointed out, it’s all part of the media’s effort to create a “permission structure” to defend Trump, despite the clear danger he poses to democracy.**
At COURIER, we don’t play into this false “both sides” narrative. Our reporting focuses on the truth: Trump is dangerous and a threat to our democracy. The legacy media’s failure to cover him properly is part of the reason he rose to power in the first place.

### Meanwhile, Netanyahu advances plans to annex Gaza in continued violation of international law

Recent revelations from _Haaretz_ , Israel's longest-running newspaper, have confirmed a deeply disturbing reality: [Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has actively blocked every potential hostage deal since October 7th, 2023](https://substack.com/redirect/bc9fd2a8-b712-4fea-b26e-832dcc54c0b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). While the public narrative continues to ask why Hamas refuses to agree to such deals, the more pressing question is why Netanyahu himself has repeatedly obstructed these opportunities, and why the West continues to arm him? The answer to these questions speak to a much darker truth. **Let 's Address This.**
**Let's Address This with Qasim Rashid is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..9HwAXLbtcJHorWHruewmDkUVZ8wqrE8plsWhOaRsMio?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=150450079)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/52ea13da-cccf-4cd6-8858-71718c186973?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Haaretz and the Jewish Independent both cite the report by _[Channel 12 News'](https://substack.com/redirect/b428621d-92f3-4930-99c1-cf56fa72cfbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ Yaron Avraham, that](https://substack.com/redirect/b428621d-92f3-4930-99c1-cf56fa72cfbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> Since the hostage release-ceasefire deal in November, Israel's negotiation team has been a [futile mission to secure another deal](https://substack.com/redirect/f4fcd8b8-1be8-42c0-a43a-0b35399b7b36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to bring home more hostages, while Netanyahu "_did everything in his power to make sure they are not successful_ ". Netanyahu walked back several promises he made, including an agreement to end the war, and invented new "non-starters" that were previously never mentioned that blocked a deal. He also repeatedly prevented negotiators from travelling to ceasefire talks, or greatly limited their negotiation powers when they are allowed to go.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9a42257b-a743-4e46-b27f-e50ec37c6949?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But perhaps even more concerning is that this is not a recent development. Haaretz reported way back in March, 2024, that [Netanyahu's own generals are angry with him for "sabotaging a hostage deal](https://substack.com/redirect/f4fcd8b8-1be8-42c0-a43a-0b35399b7b36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." In fact, the families of the hostages themselves [condemn Netanyahu as "Mr. Death](https://substack.com/redirect/aa98fa32-9a6b-4144-8506-e8f49642254f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," stating that they learned [a full hostage deal was on the table in October of 2023, that Netanyahu rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/0e4fef4b-4402-411e-b847-894bce2a601b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1eed539f-c55f-42fc-b8a7-b66a0b24fcb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..9HwAXLbtcJHorWHruewmDkUVZ8wqrE8plsWhOaRsMio?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=150450079)
Simultaneously, [Netanyahu has made clear his intention to annex Gaza](https://substack.com/redirect/87aa201d-00dd-4b01-baa9-94ef61a962d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), further deepening the catastrophe that already grips the Palestinian territory. This is not a random byproduct of war--it is a deliberate strategy to seize land that does not belong to Israel under international law. It is no different in practical effect than Putin annexing part of The Ukraine. Meanwhile, the Israeli military continues to bombard Gaza, killing civilians indiscriminately. How, then, can anyone deny that this is the perpetuation of genocide?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/24b30afa-992b-4c3c-a03e-12aff8552c98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Indeed, one of the most difficult elements to prove when assessing genocide is the matter of intent. Yet what other conclusion can be drawn when Netanyahu blocks hostage deals, prolongs the conflict, and openly declares his plans to annex Gaza while it lies in ruins? This is not accidental. This is calculated. This is _intentional_. And it does not take an international human rights lawyer to see the intent behind this cruelty.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..9HwAXLbtcJHorWHruewmDkUVZ8wqrE8plsWhOaRsMio?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=150450079)
One of the most effective propaganda claims Netanyahu has disseminated is that "he'd stop bombing Gaza if only Hamas would accept releasing all hostages." Meanwhile, as the receipts in this article shows, Netanyahu has been the main culprit behind preventing a hostage deal, even as he rejected [UN Security Council Resolution 2735](https://substack.com/redirect/43789ae2-e56d-4386-ad72-8562344a9f3d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). UNSC 2735 is a binding UN resolution of Israel's own hostage release proposal, and [Netanyahu rejected it once it passed ](https://substack.com/redirect/fefec17d-ba88-4d1f-814f-04797ee7b69b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[because](https://substack.com/redirect/fefec17d-ba88-4d1f-814f-04797ee7b69b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ Hamas accepted it](https://substack.com/redirect/fefec17d-ba88-4d1f-814f-04797ee7b69b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7e06227a-5e94-4f8f-a903-ece97b96ddfe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And now, Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar is dead, killed by the Israeli military. VP Harris has reissued her calls for an end to the siege on Gaza. And while I would love nothing more than to be proven wrong--I am betting that Netanyahu will not stop his siege.
Enough is enough. It is past time for the international community to stop arming Netanyahu's regime and enabling these crimes. The siege on Gaza must end, and those responsible for these atrocities--Netanyahu and his military generals--must be held accountable. Only through justice and accountability can we ensure true safety and security for both Palestinians and Israelis, in both the short and long term.

In fact, the families of the hostages themselves ," stating that they learned . | | ---|---|--- Simultaneously, , further deepening the catastrophe that already grips the Palestinian territory. This is not a random byproduct of war--it is a deliberate strategy to seize land that does not belong to Israel under international law. It is no different in practical effect than Putin annexing part of The Ukraine. Meanwhile, the Israeli military continues to bombard Gaza, killing civilians indiscriminately. How, then, can anyone deny that this is the perpetuation of genocide? | | ---|---|--- Indeed, one of the most difficult elements to prove when assessing genocide is the matter of intent. Yet what other conclusion can be drawn when Netanyahu blocks hostage deals, prolongs the conflict, and openly declares his plans to annex Gaza while it lies in ruins? This is not accidental. This is calculated. This is intentional. And it does not take an international human rights lawyer to see the intent behind this cruelty. One of the most effective propaganda claims Netanyahu has disseminated is that "he'd stop bombing Gaza if only Hamas would accept releasing all hostages." Meanwhile, as the receipts in this article shows, Netanyahu has been the main culprit behind preventing a hostage deal, even as he rejected . UNSC 2735 is a binding UN resolution of Israel's own hostage release proposal, and . | | ---|---|--- And now, Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar is dead, killed by the Israeli military. VP Harris has reissued her calls for an end to the siege on Gaza. And while I would love nothing more than to be proven wrong--I am betting that Netanyahu will not stop his siege. Enough is enough. It is past time for the international community to stop arming Netanyahu's regime and enabling these crimes. The siege on Gaza must end, and those responsible for these atrocities--Netanyahu and his military generals--must be held accountable. Only through justice and accountability can we ensure true safety and security for both Palestinians and Israelis, in both the short and long term. ## The Last Lap
---
Yesterday, I spoke in **Salem, North Carolina** at the **ReAwaken America Tour**. This is city number 24 on the Tour. Hard to believe we have visited 24 cities in less than 3 years. But this stop was different. **It is the FINAL city.** I am so grateful to have been given the opportunity to join **Team America** and do our part to help Save America. I want to thank **Clay Clark** , **General Michael Flynn** and **Eric Trump** for the _opportunity of a lifetime_! Let's go **WIN** in November. Be sure to drag your friends and family to the polls and **vote for Donald J. Trump!** God Bless America! Pastor Jackson Lahmeyer

Derek, take a
look at this photo that I found.

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=oct2024_abs_em.0Y0BaT&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_GEN_AC90_20241019_PM1_V1_S1&t=1004&akid=7841%2E5257348%2EDJkWY9 ]Adam as a young boy

That young kid with the missing front teeth and curious look? That’s me!

If you had told him he’d grow up to run for the U.S. Senate from
California, he’d probably be thrilled — and definitely surprised.

You see, growing up, I was fascinated by history and politics.

Sitting around the dinner table at night, my family would talk about the
news of the day or the history book my father was reading at the moment.

The conversations at our family table were always lively — my dad came
from a long line of Democrats, while my mom’s side was deeply Republican
(her father was even a Republican County chairman). You can just imagine!

Back then, Democrats and Republicans often disagreed, but there was mutual
respect. They could debate without turning hostile.

So, what changed? A lot. The way we consume information, cable news, and
algorithms are designed to fuel anger and division.

And then Donald Trump became President. He didn’t just divide us; he used
old tactics like bigotry and hate while inventing new ways to pit us
against each other.

When I first entered politics, Democrats and Republicans still worked
together to get things done. Disagreements were common, but they always
prioritized the American people and found common ground. And still find a
way to seek out others across the aisle and deliver for California.

But those days when I was growing up seem quaint now. We have seen a
seismic shift in the last few years — since a charlatan celebrity and
reality TV host who called disabled veterans “suckers” and “losers,”
denigrated our immigrant communities, and railed on about “fake news” was
elected President of the United States.

But I’ve never backed down from bullies. So, I took on Donald Trump — not
because it was easy, but because it was necessary.

And for standing up, I’ve become one of Trump’s favorite targets.

The little boy in that picture never would have imagined being attacked by
a U.S. President and his allies.

But if defending democracy, our rights, and the Constitution makes me an
enemy of Trump and the MAGA movement, I’ll proudly wear that badge.

These are the battles I’ll continue to fight in the U.S. Senate, where
many of Trump’s biggest enablers still reside. That’s why he’s doing
everything to stop me.

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=oct2024_abs_em.0Y0BaT&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_GEN_AC90_20241019_PM1_V1_S1&email=&amount=10&t=1005&akid=7841%2E5257348%2EDJkWY9 ]With just weeks until November 5th, we have little time to waste if

### **Expect the Unexpected!
**
---
Hillary Clinton recently commented that there would be an October surprise that would upend the election. We can’t begin to speculate what she was referring to, but really, no one knows what the future holds.

**_This election has been a lesson in life’s unpredictability_** _.
_
Who would have guessed that Kamala and Minnesota’s own Governor Walz would be on the Democratic ticket and Trump would have been the target of two assassination attempts?

In recent weeks, we’ve watched natural disasters sweep across the Southeast, leaving millions of people, even some living miles above sea level, underwater and dealing with unimaginable losses.

So, how does an unpredictable election or surprise natural disaster impact our decisions this election? First, we’ve seen that leadership matters. Sadly, regardless of the election outcome, our country will likely remain divided. _Congress will have an important leadership role in advancing sound policies to unite us and set us on a better path forward.
_
I’m running for Congress because I believe this country could use a steady hand right now. If you’ve seen my weekly emails, I’ve laid out the case for why my nonpartisan and bipartisan public service would allow me to be an experienced, common-sense voice in Congress, and I hope I have your support.

But that’s not why I’m reaching out to you today. **Given life’s unpredictability, would you consider voting early?
**
**_Did you know you as of October 18 th, you can go to an early voting center and submit your ballot right into a voting machine_?** You can be assured that your vote will be counted.

It probably won’t be a hurricane that prevents you from getting to the polls on election day (now that would be unexpected and historic!), but it could be a flat tire or a sick child. Recent events have taught us to expect the unexpected.

**This is not an election any of us can afford to miss. Vote now, and encourage your friends and family to vote early, too.**

body:
As president of our local union, I led the strike.
_[Click here to stop receiving emails about Dan Osborn's campaign in Nebraska from us.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95384613/506545153/1647001491?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjIxNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNThkOWZmNC00MzhlLWVmMTEtODQ3NC0wMDBkM2E5OGZhNmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=h7-HOei1MOHvJsz25b1TrjOcbuniaasHG6QjWdZ5i04=&emci=9d664b2d-c68d-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&emdi=a58d9ff4-438e-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&ceid=19445147)_
Hey there,
In October 2021, I had been an employee of Kellogg’s for almost 18 years.
I had dropped out of college and gone to work for the company after my wife got pregnant. Life’s easy when all you gotta do is take care of yourself – but we had diapers to buy and needed health insurance for our growing family.
When I applied in 2004, there were 6 positions and 600 applications. Working at Kellogg’s promised to be a lifelong career. A good-paying job that afforded me the opportunity to become a homeowner, let my wife stay home with the kids, live decently, retire some day, and hopefully live happily ever after.
But over the years, wages became a two-tier system. New workers were being paid less than workers had made decades earlier. Cost of living adjustments weren’t keeping up anywhere near inflation. Retirement and health insurance plans had been gutted. It just wasn’t right. They were making record profits – and doing it off the backs of workers.
**So in October 2021, we walked out. And as president of our local union, I led the strike.**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95384614/506545154/92586991?refcode=em20241019mid2-nd&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C35%2C50%2C100%2C250&refcode2=a58d9ff4-438e-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&recurring=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjIxNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNThkOWZmNC00MzhlLWVmMTEtODQ3NC0wMDBkM2E5OGZhNmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=h7-HOei1MOHvJsz25b1TrjOcbuniaasHG6QjWdZ5i04=)
It was the first time many of us had ever walked a picket line. It was cold, but we were determined to hold our lines even through the dead of the winter if we had to. Every worker knew we were a part of something bigger than ourselves. We were in a fight for the future of the American middle class.
After 11 weeks, and the company threatening to permanently replace every union worker, we reached an agreement. More importantly, we saved 500 good-paying jobs here in Nebraska alone.
It was one of the proudest moments of my life.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95384617/506545158/92586991?refcode=em20241019mid2-nd&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C35%2C50%2C100%2C250&refcode2=a58d9ff4-438e-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&recurring=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjIxNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNThkOWZmNC00MzhlLWVmMTEtODQ3NC0wMDBkM2E5OGZhNmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=h7-HOei1MOHvJsz25b1TrjOcbuniaasHG6QjWdZ5i04=)
Following the strike, I was fired. The company has its version of events for why, but I believe it was because I was union president. Someone had to pay – and my head was on the chopping block.
It’s easy to let yourself get beaten down by life. To let big corporations and the politicians they own in Washington make all the decisions – and just accept that that’s how things will always be. But that’s not me.
**Instead, I’ve decided to run against one of the most corporate politicians – U.S. Senator Republican Deb Fischer – and with your help, we are going to defeat her.**
Five brand-new polls show me narrowly LEADING Republican Deb Fischer, and according to experts at FiveThirtyEight, Nebraska is now the CLOSEST Senate race in the entire country.
**I am taking on Republican Senator Deb Fischer just like I took on Kellogg’s. But I sure as hell am not taking money from corporate PACs, so I need grassroots donors like you to give now if we’re going to win this Senate seat.**
**[Please, will you make a donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate right now – whatever you can afford – to help me defeat Republican Deb Fischer and win this Senate seat in November?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95384624/506545161/92586991?refcode=em20241019mid2-nd&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C35%2C50%2C100%2C250&refcode2=a58d9ff4-438e-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&recurring=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjIxNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNThkOWZmNC00MzhlLWVmMTEtODQ3NC0wMDBkM2E5OGZhNmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=h7-HOei1MOHvJsz25b1TrjOcbuniaasHG6QjWdZ5i04=)**

Dear Peter,
Almost everyone knows a friend, a family member, or a community member whose life has been touched by abuse. This thread of resilience that connects nearly all of us is the reason we joined the [**_Survivors for Kamala coalition._**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/95386386/506550942/128264743?ms=101924_survivorsforkamala&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNV08vMS83NjczNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwNDY0Y2EyNi00ODhlLWVmMTEtODQ3NC0wMDBkM2E5OGZhNmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=429lWSfe0N9ZFl2pt1l4XXLgN3K2T-bso0BqA1NWq2A=&emci=7f1637b9-818d-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&emdi=0464ca26-488e-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&ceid=864787)
We all have different stories, but at this crucial moment, we share one message: that **Kamala Harris is the only option in this election** ; that **Donald Trump is an adjudicated abuser** ; and that the time has come to **stand strong for our lives and our freedom.**
Survivors deserve better.
_America_ deserves better.

This thread of resilience that connects nearly all of us is the reason we joined the We all have different stories, but at this crucial moment, we share one message: that Kamala Harris is the only option in this election ; that Donald Trump is an adjudicated abuser ; and that the time has come to stand strong for our lives and our freedom. Survivors deserve better. America deserves better. We know that this is a challenging topic to discuss, even with the closest family and friends — but we firmly believe that we build strength in community, and that by working together to support a candidate who will champion our cause, we can help create policies that ensure safety, justice, and healing for all survivors. In solidarity, Care in Action

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jill Stein for President 2024
body:
Did you miss these latest shenanigans?

| | | [ ](jillstein2024.com/)
---
Peter, We sent out an email about the so-called "Voters Of Tomorrow" group that you may have missed. We want to make sure you know who this shady organization is and what they are up to in case you see their videos on social media. They’re a group that claims to speak for Gen Z and prop up the anti-Democratic Party. But they’re not particularly popular with Gen Z or anyone else, judging by the fact that their posts and videos get very few views, shares and likes.

Here is where it gets interesting: NBC News released an article trumpeting a video from Voters Of Tomorrow attacking Jill, perfectly timed to coincide with the videos launch. It seems odd that NBC would amplify the voice of such an obscure group and was ready to promote their smear as soon as it came out. _**Coincidence? We think not.**_

Guy Christensen, well-known on social media as Your Favorite Guy, has some thoughts on the matter. Guy is also Gen Z, and his videos are wildly popular with young people because he’s lending his powerful voice to their righteous anger over the genocide in Gaza that the Biden-Harris administration has been funding to the tune of billions of dollars and massive weapon transfers to Israel for over a year. Check out Guy’s video responding to the coordinated attack on Jill here:

Team Stein/Ware is thrilled that Guy has recently joined us because he knows that Jill and Butch are the only choice for young people who are standing up for the people of Gaza and demanding an end to this horrific genocide.

Our campaign’s people-powered platform is speaking to issues that this incredible younger generation cares deeply about: from our strong stand against genocide to our real Green New Deal that seriously addresses the climate emergency threatening their futures, to fighting for living wages, debt-free education, and Medicare For All.

Jill and Butch have the mouthpieces for empire in the corporate media running scared, and as we get closer to the election, they’re amping up their smear campaigns - like giving a national media platform to irrelevant groups like Voters Of Tomorrow in the hopes that they can sell them as the voice of America’s youth.[_**

At midnight, we will hit our critical midnight fundraising deadline, which will set the tone for our campaign's capacity to get out the vote with less than 17 days until the election. [If you’re ready to give now without having to hear any more, you can chip in a split donation of $10 or more between Ritchie Torres and my campaign right now.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95386515/506551144/-1242516620?amount=10&refcode=RTFC_20241019_EMSPL_E1_T0_AC&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmOTliYTkyMC00ODhlLWVmMTEtODQ3NC0wMDBkM2E5OGZhNmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rv88Q2CV4SlozjNXlIjupa4i22CZFdtXe-gAIPDtWAI=)

# **JD Vance is Weird**
---
| | | | | [ ](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2v50cw-fk0hv9-kyd76rh8/)
---
| | | | folks, Let's face it: JD Vance is weird. Saying that political leaders without biological children "don't really have a direct stake" in the country is outlandish, to say the least. His odd viewpoints alienate a significant portion of the population and raise questions about Vance's grasp on reality. The Democrats' new strategy of labeling Trump and Vance as weird seems to be working brilliantly. We have seen in the media that it frustrates opponents, leading them to amplify it further with their off-balance responses. So far, Trump and Vance have been incapable of finding an effective comeback, leaving them scrambling. Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, a potential vice-presidential candidate for Harris, called Trump and Vance "just weird" in a recent interview. The Democratic Governors Association amplified this sentiment, spreading it across social media. Walz even referenced Trump's bizarre habit of mentioning the fictional serial killer Hannibal Lecter from "Silence of the Lambs" in his stump speeches, adding to the weirdness factor. Harris's campaign hasn't missed a beat in highlighting Vance's oddities. In a recent news release, they described Vance's out-of-touch ideas, particularly his stance on abortion and his comments about childless leaders. Harris allies, including Sens. Brian Schatz of Hawaii and Chris Murphy of Connecticut, have also chimed in, calling Vance's past comments "super weird." At her first fundraiser as the likely Democratic nominee, Harris herself called out Trump's "wild lies" and Vance's peculiar statements, reiterating that the only box to put them in is "weird." This new narrative has given Democrats a powerful advantage, one they rarely had when President Biden was still in the race. JD Vance's weirdness isn't a new revelation, either. While the majority of the public is learning who Vance is for the first time through these strange headlines, he has a history of making controversial remarks. In a 2021 interview, Vance slammed prominent childless Democrats, including Harris, as "childless cat ladies" with no stake in America. This comment alone is enough to raise eyebrows and question his judgment. Harris's quip in 2018, when preparing for a potential debate with Trump, sums it up perfectly: "Why are you being so weird? What's wrong with you?" Despite their attempts to flip the script, Trump and Vance have struggled. Trump spokesman Steven Cheung's attempts to redirect the weird label back at Harris and her allies have fallen flat. Donald Trump Jr.'s online rants about "soft on crime" politicians and Vance's reposting of videos criticizing Harris only highlight their desperation. In contrast, Democrats have masterfully co-opted Republican attack lines, using the "weird" label to their advantage. The Republicans' previous tactics of sharing clips of Harris's laugh or her stories have backfired, with Democrats now embracing these moments as in-jokes. The "coconut tree" anecdote has even become a symbol of unity among Harris's supporters. [**_JD Vance's weirdness is not just a political talking point—_**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2v50cw-fk0hva-kyd76rh8/)[** _Vance and MAGA are clearly out of touch with what Americans want, but that does not mean they are backing down this Novemb_**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2v50cw-fk0hvb-kyd76rh9/) [**_er. We need to fight MAG_**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2v50cw-fk0hvc-kyd76rh0/)[** _https://secure.actblue.com/donate/no-dem-left-behind-pac-1?refcode=cm_**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2v50cw-fk0hvd-kyd76rh1/) [**_A in all 50 states and send them home for good in 2024!_**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2v50cw-fk0hve-kyd76rh2/)

I’ve been called racial slurs by plenty of “tolerant” leftists who say Black Lives Matter.
But being called a “raisin” in a “potato salad” is a new low I never thought possible.
It’s Byron Donalds, I was on Bill Maher’s show in July when one of his Woke guests had the audacity to call me a “raisin” inside the GOP’s “potato salad” straight to my face.
These people hate to see that our movement isn’t bound by their narrow-minded views on race.
**THEY HATE that I’m a Black Man who supports President Trump.**
And the saddest of all, they think Black folks everywhere shouldn’t think for themselves and should vote Democrat for the rest of their lives.
I can’t believe this is the case, but if folks like him get their way this November, things will only get worse.
Democrats are surging in fundraising after Kamala took the reins, raising over $90 million in 24 hours after her announcement.
They’ve never been in a better position to crush us.

| | Team — In a truly weird turn of events, Donald Trump came to Coachella, California, for a campaign rally with less than 25 days to go in this election. And instead of focusing his speech on telling people what he’d do as president, he spent a lot of his time attacking me in terms we only hear from dictators. Here’s just a small sample of what he said about yours truly: _**“Sleazebag”
“Major lowlife”
“A bad person, a sick person”**_ Yet again, this is just more of the same attacks he throws at me every chance he gets. Whether he’s at a rally in Iowa, Pennsylvania, Florida, or right here in California, he just can’t stop thinking about me. But that’s not all he said. He attacked California’s election integrity, setting up future claims of election fraud when he inevitably loses our state. In the midst of [an ongoing series](https://substack.com/redirect/d0e72805-34b2-469c-8bc1-1d3f90cedcc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) addressing Israel's expansion of its violent aggression across the Middle East even beyond the horrific ongoing genocide of Gaza, this post focuses on a narrower theme: municipal elections in San Francisco.
_Thanks for reading Chronicles of a Dying Empire! This post is public, and covers a set of issues widely ignored --and actively suppressed--by professional journalists. You can help inform your friends by sharing it._
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1018597&post_id=150451285&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTUwNDUxMjg1LCJpYXQiOjE3MjkzNjUwMTQsImV4cCI6MTczMTk1NzAxNCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwMTg1OTciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.CF7fDkxLqtbqb93qInqjRPe7Hrnxv4V4GxI7xJ_KpqM)
Because it examines the political culture from which the Democratic nominee for the presidency emerged, as well as the former Speaker of the House, this post also has implications for the national Democratic party and its [hypocrisy with respect to race and inclusion](https://substack.com/redirect/13bcd876-71e3-4f16-aba7-0367641829da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Finally, this post is relevant to news media, the historic failures of journalists, and their ongoing susceptibility to parroting the talking points of elites, rather than observing reality or checking facts.
To question whether an individual leader in the United States is racist is like asking whether human beings breathe air, or alternatively, whether bears shit in the woods.
### Hypocrisy comes at a cost
Observing the presidential race, _The New York Times_ [published](https://substack.com/redirect/025c2cf0-c0e0-4b08-a04f-19dd43fea0b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the following passage on Monday morning:
> _" The past four years have highlighted the ways that Democrats exaggerate the political importance of racial identity. Joe Biden, after all, promised to nominate the first Black female Supreme Court justice (which he did) and chose Kamala Harris as the first Black vice president -- who has now succeeded him as the Democratic nominee. Yet Harris has less support from Black voters than Hillary Clinton did in 2016._
> _Biden also adopted the sort of welcoming immigration policies that Democrats have long believed Hispanic voters support. He loosened border rules early in his term, which helped millions of people enter the country. In spite of that change -- or maybe partly because of it -- Democrats have also lost Hispanic support._
> _Harris is still winning most voters of color. But the Democratic Party typically needs landslide margins among these groups to win elections. Today, a significant share of them view the Democratic Party with deep skepticism -- roughly one in five Black voters, two in five Hispanic voters and one in three Asian voters, polls suggest."_
Even while observing the erosion of support for Democrats among communities of color, reporters remain unwilling to report established facts or acknowledge the disturbing reality that Democrats have proven to be as racist as Republicans, and no less committed to guarding Wall Street from the demands of working class Americans struggling to survive.
It's almost as if an entire political culture forgot its own history, and the [legacy of a national hero](https://substack.com/redirect/959143c8-88d6-4753-8cd6-ff7dbb9ee89c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) whose likeness is carved in stone in the nation's capital.
### **What white supremacy & racism mean**
I have [explained many times](https://substack.com/redirect/443c22d9-8b3b-4eda-8e4c-8dd3fe975995?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in many forums that most Americans conflate racism and prejudice, not understanding the significant difference between the two concepts, or how they relate to white supremacy.
Prejudice is rooted in interpersonal bias. It embodies unfairness, runs contrary to our nation's stated ideals, and limits the prospects of individuals by enabling pernicious discrimination. Yet, relative to racism, the impact of prejudice is fairly limited.
Racism, in contrast, is a systematized hierarchy that characterizes not individuals, but the entire society that embraces it. As [MLK explained](https://substack.com/redirect/aa286970-195f-4347-9d33-646ce195821f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), racism operates alongside capitalism and militarism to entrench public support for international violence and imperialism. It is enabled not only by prejudice and hate, but also by opportunism and power.
Ironically, racism is less about race and denigrating people of a particular race than it is about promoting people of the dominant background, and insulating capital from social or political challenges. After all, unapologetic racists tend to pursue an equal opportunity version of hatred: it is not particularly any race that they disfavor, but rather all of them, other than their own. That suggests that their uniting principle is not the race that they target for hate in any given instance, but rather the one they defend.
That's why white supremacy tends to be a better descriptor of right wing racism than merely "racism," which most Americans, and particularly its critics, fail to understand.
For instance, any number of professional writers have penned articles that [question whether Donald Trump is a racist](https://substack.com/redirect/75ae5b9d-a1f1-4077-8e46-a42626a73d5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Trump is certainly a white supremacist, and a shameless one, at that. That much is as clear from his actions and his governance record as from his recent words.
But to question whether an individual leader in the United States is racist is like asking whether a human being breathes air and drinks water, or alternatively, whether bears shit in the woods.
In sad fact, this entire country is racist: from its top to its bottom, from its [origins](https://substack.com/redirect/0d4a90c6-4dbf-4813-8483-cc544572fca4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the current [moment](https://substack.com/redirect/17334066-18e3-499e-b943-c4969a25a2a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), from left to right, from [republican to democrat](https://substack.com/redirect/805e3157-9275-46fe-9622-eb5f9e0fd359?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), from rich to poor, from west to east, and from San Francisco to Miami.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c17c4305-a1bb-4bb7-883e-29a06bb5e83b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Questioning whether an individual is racist is a chimera. The question aims to probe whether leaders wield prejudice. But frankly, that's not even terribly significant: mere deference to the established system allows the far more pernicious threat of institutionalized racism to flourish and expand. The only commitment from a public official that would carry any meaning is to actively dismantle racism, but the number of voices in federal elected office who have made that commitment can be counted on one hand.

### **A surprising --and revealing--endorsement**
San Francisco's Board of Supervisors is the equivalent of a municipal legislature, since San Francisco has the unique distinction in California of being both a city and a county.
Among the sitting supervisors on the Board, one is generally described as a socialist, despite coming from a wealthy family, living in a mansion, and playing a critical role in entrenching a corrupt national leader of the corporate Democratic Party. His name is Dean Preston, and he represents District 5, in which I used to live while running for Congress in 2020 and 2022. The district encompasses the historic Haight-Ashbury neighborhood, and was recently redistricted to also include parts of the Tenderloin, an area renowned for urban blight and any number of social challenges from visible homelessness to addiction and mental health crisis.
In July, Preston was [endorsed](https://substack.com/redirect/68a3c36e-44e4-4324-b27d-b32a4ffb7cb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by House speaker emerita Nancy Pelosi, even though their policy visions appear as if they could not be more diametrically opposed.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d327f48c-3577-424e-8faa-70a3d26c4ce5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Preston has built a public reputation around advocating for affordable housing (while repeatedly impeding market-rate construction projects). In contrast, Pelosi is an [unapologetically corrupt](https://substack.com/redirect/be82fbd8-f4e0-416c-82cc-02feeae9ca26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) plutocrat who has used her seat in Congress as a way of securing inside information to leverage in her stock market portfolio, through which she has gained over $200 million during her time in office. Her legacy also includes the historic privatization of [previously federal land](https://substack.com/redirect/43ffb9b3-006d-4953-b7a0-b18b1459d3b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in San Francisco, and she has responded to concerns about social equity with a flippant rejoinder dismissing them: "[We are capitalists](https://substack.com/redirect/abd75eec-abaf-4cdb-942f-dc46e3772a49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)."
When Pelosi endorsed Preston, a great many people scratched their heads, curious why an oligarch with a focus on national politics would deign to endorse a local politician whose vision has so frequently challenged her own.
Pelosi endorsed Preston to reward party loyalty. But not a single writer in San Francisco possesses the independence to observe how Preston earned it.
It is remarkable to witness a major city, from which both the Democratic nominee for the presidency and the former House Speaker emerged, without a single reporter sufficiently independent to observe the obvious answer to so simple a question.
### **What no one else has the independence to observe **
Pelosi endorsed Preston for a simple reason: he emerged as her most crucial political ally in 2020 by [falsely accusing](https://substack.com/redirect/93426ef1-e92d-4e23-8eb6-c815d17a9b31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the only viable challenger Pelosi has ever faced--me--of various sorts of misconduct.
The [character assassination](https://substack.com/redirect/51a40817-7a91-4551-8121-55cebdc5287f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that doomed my 2020 campaign, and eventually chased me out of San Francisco, was shameless, orchestrated in bad faith, and enabled by institutional actors across the Democratic Party, as well as journalists who continue to falsely claim independence from it.
It was quintessentially public, organized specifically to mislead journalists and subvert the integrity of San Francisco's most contested federal election since 1987. Yet a city of nearly 1,000,000 people seems to have forgotten the disinformation promoted by several of its elected leaders in the service of entrenching the most powerful among them.
Pelosi endorsed Preston to reward party loyalty. But not a single writer in San Francisco possesses the independence to observe how Preston earned it.
Why have reporters ignored what should be obvious to anyone paying attention?
Perhaps because they made themselves complicit themselves in a racist smear campaign orchestrated to mislead voters and undermine a federal election, and denied themselves the opportunity to reflect on local politics without implicating their own professional interests. There's a reason why the only professional [journalists](https://substack.com/redirect/a2468140-bc30-4935-ad83-0928aa5e8571?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to [explicitly](https://substack.com/redirect/93426ef1-e92d-4e23-8eb6-c815d17a9b31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) observe the racism implicit in my character assassination all live outside San Francisco.
### **Who cares?**
It's not merely the case that Preston helped orchestrated a disinformation campaign that skewed the results of a congressional election, insulated the corrupt leadership of a corporate political party that was [on the ropes at the time](https://substack.com/redirect/b49ee9f4-ad57-4a29-aa20-e15754d1fdcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and lied to the public.
For what it's worth, Preston was far from alone: other figures who plotted to mislead the public and subvert the integrity of a federal election with [weaponized racist lies](https://substack.com/redirect/8ec1f895-abfb-4d4c-97a5-2e998de75f16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) included several former campaign staff who had been removed from our campaign after I won the 2020 primary, particularly [Jasper Wilde and Emily Jones](https://substack.com/redirect/7ae9a73b-bba6-410f-b129-384812efacfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); Jackie Thornhill, who was at the time working as an aide to San Francisco Supervisor Raphael Mandelman and on the Board of an LGBTQ Democratic club whose disturbing and [recurring white supremacy](https://substack.com/redirect/63bbb081-de4d-4277-9d13-237b333f7e9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has been publicly recognized by several of its recent past presidents; and [Brandon Harami](https://substack.com/redirect/1c314c7d-e393-40b5-8d6a-c2f64d1b4145?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the current Chief of Staff to Sheng Thao, the embattled Mayor of Oakland facing a federal [investigation for corruption](https://substack.com/redirect/581cab5b-7a12-42b4-9f18-d4d54f983bd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
In the time since he smeared me, Preston's district was expanded to include the Tenderloin, one of San Francisco's most diverse neighborhoods. Preston's public racism and white supremacy deserve to be documented, but because writers across San Francisco have unfortunately shared it, they lack the independence to publicly observe it.
One journalist--who revealingly chose to remain anonymous--even [admitted](https://substack.com/redirect/bc70908e-f179-4313-b1f8-a46b11f98af7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the _California Globe_ that he & others published premature articles privileging false claims about me based on nothing more than baseless accusations aimed at subverting an election.
> [A] lot of us published first without waiting to see who else came forward. Turns out it was no one, and people were hurt in the process, including political campaigns....[M]any journalists were caught up in the [#metoo] movement at the time and believed accusers because so many had gone on for so long without ever being believed. But, as we've seen, it really goes both ways."
The various publications that smeared me failed to pursue any modicum of fact checking. Some have [implicitly acknowledged their errors](https://substack.com/redirect/9344ac48-c807-4259-97a3-cf68400dd4c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by publishing subsequent stories calling into question their previous articles that ultimately insulated corporate control over the Democratic Party by allowing Nancy Pelosi to duck debates despite [public demands](https://substack.com/redirect/745b3d87-6912-4909-9fcf-38aec33aae81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for one.
In fact, it appears that the _San Francisco Chronicle_ 's front-page coverage of [Pelosi's history of ducking debates](https://substack.com/redirect/cf740e81-e9b7-4c05-859d-12008e222bb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) played a key role in prompting my character assassination, which followed a week later. Yet none have retracted or corrected any of their stories based on the racist lies that they now acknowledge anonymously.
In fact, those stories, ignored evidence, suppressed [whistleblowers](https://substack.com/redirect/7ae9a73b-bba6-410f-b129-384812efacfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), mischaracterized their experiences, and led to them being smeared, themselves.
Even _the Intercept_ , which once prided itself on bringing the stories of whistleblowers to light, suppressed whistleblowers who tried to exposed the corruption of journalism and politics in San Francisco, and ultimately reinforced it. Writer Akela Lacy initially amplified the racist plot orchestrated by Preston and others, and even after the publication revised its story four times in two months (all without public corrections or retractions), continued to mischaracterize whistleblowers, their roles in the city, their roles on our campaign, and their observations of the orchestration of lies that Lacy published. After one of the whistleblowers faced retaliatory smears, herself, she went on to publish her own reflections in [the San Francisco Bayview](https://substack.com/redirect/7ae9a73b-bba6-410f-b129-384812efacfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
How is a sitting member of the Board of Supervisors poised to potentially win reelection and represent a minority community in America's "mOsT pRoGrEsSiVe" city without any public discussion of his history of white supremacy?
### But what about Harris?
Anyone familiar with San Francisco politics, the ascent of Kamala Harris, and Nancy Pelosi's role in the Democratic Party, should frankly not be surprised by this history.
There are plenty of opportunities for people of color even in racist systems, as long as they support capital and militarism.
Some might imagine that, because Harris is herself a person of color from San Francisco currently serving in the White House, the city must not have a problem with race. After all, if the city can send the first female, Black, or Asian Vice President to Washington, how could San Francisco possibly embody racism or white supremacy?
They key lies in recalling what racism and white supremacy mean. There are plenty of opportunities for people of color even in racist systems, as long as they support capital and militarism. That is precisely what Harris has done across her entire career. She came to Washington after years working as a predatory prosecutor, embodying domestic militarism. And while she is depicted by journalists as if she were a progressive, Harris has signaled her [allegiance to Wall Street](https://substack.com/redirect/2af7b9c0-669f-4cb2-a733-4e08fc8ec213?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as part of her presidential campaign.
Voices of color who challenge the political orthodoxy that Harris has always embraced endure a remarkably different experience in San Francisco.
### **A proudly "progressive" racist city**
San Francisco enjoys a reputation as one of the country's most progressive cities, largely because of the cities, cultural legacy, and the relative prominence of LGBTQ voices within the city's political establishment.
But the city's racist history looms in the background, and was firmly established long before I was subjected to it.
In a previous era, Chinese Americans were [viciously targeted](https://substack.com/redirect/e9a049a2-80df-45d6-86b0-6517a8d554b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with violence, discrimination, and hate.
More recently, Latinos have suffered indignities ranging from [arbitrary police violence](https://substack.com/redirect/d00e41e5-e994-4476-bd33-b0524ea5c149?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to gentrification and [random harassment](https://substack.com/redirect/c0a59349-4e60-4f64-916d-c13464430917?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by fellow San Franciscans.
San Francisco's Black communities, meanwhile, have been eviscerated through a combination of aggressive policing and [gentrification](https://substack.com/redirect/258da137-cc00-4f9a-a447-02f876e2739f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) imposed by a brutal housing market. They have also endured one of the most vicious, pernicious, and long-standing examples of environmental racism anywhere in the United States.
The Hunters Point shipyard was the site where the Pentagon assembled nuclear bombs ultimately detonated on civilian populations in Japan. But the only weapons of mass destruction in our species' history used intentionally to kill civilians didn't only kill hundreds of thousands of Japanese people [only to send a message](https://substack.com/redirect/d34a7c2d-3842-4261-a2bc-b5cd09366c0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). They also [poisoned](https://substack.com/redirect/965b1497-9fae-4f4d-9f25-4170418791ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tens of thousands of San Franciscans, most of them Black, who have predictably experienced some of the highest rates of breast cancer in the world.
In 1964, author and playwright James Baldwin filmed a documentary film exposing the racism in San Francisco that remains widely unobserved.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/542b21ad-8b16-46ae-9f4e-3a27ca450073?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"Take This Hammer" documents a racist history that unfortunately continues unabated to this day. As reviewed by Richard Brody in _the New Yorker_ :
> Baldwin, guided by the social-services executive Orville Luster, interviews young black residents and learns of the massive uprooting of their neighborhoods under the guise of urban renewal. The movie's participants speak in detail about unemployment, police harassment, despair over the prospects of the civil-rights movement, and anger at their own exclusion from the city's prosperity and governance; one young man discusses his hope for violent revolution by black Americans and his belief that it can be organized. Baldwin, talking with Luster, calls white liberals "missionaries" unwilling to take risks for comprehensive change.
How little things change. Smear campaigns [continue to routinely target Muslim public servants](https://substack.com/redirect/10b5d927-df46-4194-b7a0-db067cf2801e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and reporters remain willing to do [the dirty work of white supremacy](https://substack.com/redirect/69dd303c-19a1-4a25-b291-984e787e4cfe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by indulging lies orchestrated to serve power and enabled by prejudice.
Republicans are hardly the only major American political party dedicated to white supremacy. As the voices featured in "Take This Hammer" observe, white supremacy lurks as prominently (even if less visibly) in progressive enclaves as it does in the South. Dean Preston, and the "journalists" across San Francisco who have indulged his self-serving racist lies, offer a walking case study of that unfortunate pattern.

What white supremacy & racism mean I have in many forums that most Americans conflate racism and prejudice, not understanding the significant difference between the two concepts, or how they relate to white supremacy. Prejudice is rooted in interpersonal bias. It embodies unfairness, runs contrary to our nation's stated ideals, and limits the prospects of individuals by enabling pernicious discrimination. Yet, relative to racism, the impact of prejudice is fairly limited. Racism, in contrast, is a systematized hierarchy that characterizes not individuals, but the entire society that embraces it. As , racism operates alongside capitalism and militarism to entrench public support for international violence and imperialism. It is enabled not only by prejudice and hate, but also by opportunism and power. Ironically, racism is less about race and denigrating people of a particular race than it is about promoting people of the dominant background, and insulating capital from social or political challenges. After all, unapologetic racists tend to pursue an equal opportunity version of hatred: it is not particularly any race that they disfavor, but rather all of them, other than their own. That suggests that their uniting principle is not the race that they target for hate in any given instance, but rather the one they defend. That's why white supremacy tends to be a better descriptor of right wing racism than merely "racism," which most Americans, and particularly its critics, fail to understand. Among the sitting supervisors on the Board, one is generally described as a socialist, despite coming from a wealthy family, living in a mansion, and playing a critical role in entrenching a corrupt national leader of the corporate Democratic Party. His name is Dean Preston, and he represents District 5, in which I used to live while running for Congress in 2020 and 2022. The district encompasses the historic Haight-Ashbury neighborhood, and was recently redistricted to also include parts of the Tenderloin, an area renowned for urban blight and any number of social challenges from visible homelessness to addiction and mental health crisis. In July, Preston was by House speaker emerita Nancy Pelosi, even though their policy visions appear as if they could not be more diametrically opposed. | | ---|---|--- Preston has built a public reputation around advocating for affordable housing (while repeatedly impeding market-rate construction projects). In contrast, Pelosi is an plutocrat who has used her seat in Congress as a way of securing inside information to leverage in her stock market portfolio, through which she has gained over $200 million during her time in office. Her legacy also includes the historic privatization of in San Francisco, and she has responded to concerns about social equity with a flippant rejoinder dismissing them: "." When Pelosi endorsed Preston, a great many people scratched their heads, curious why an oligarch with a focus on national politics would deign to endorse a local politician whose vision has so frequently challenged her own. Pelosi endorsed Preston to reward party loyalty. But not a single writer in San Francisco possesses the independence to observe how Preston earned it. It is remarkable to witness a major city, from which both the Democratic nominee for the presidency and the former House Speaker emerged, without a single reporter sufficiently independent to observe the obvious answer to so simple a question. What no one else has the independence to observe Pelosi endorsed Preston for a simple reason: he emerged as her most crucial political ally in 2020 by the only viable challenger Pelosi has ever faced--me--of various sorts of misconduct. The that doomed my 2020 campaign, and eventually chased me out of San Francisco, was shameless, orchestrated in bad faith, and enabled by institutional actors across the Democratic Party, as well as journalists who continue to falsely claim independence from it. It was quintessentially public, organized specifically to mislead journalists and subvert the integrity of San Francisco's most contested federal election since 1987. Yet a city of nearly 1,000,000 people seems to have forgotten the disinformation promoted by several of its elected leaders in the service of entrenching the most powerful among them. Pelosi endorsed Preston to reward party loyalty. But not a single writer in San Francisco possesses the independence to observe how Preston earned it. Why have reporters ignored what should be obvious to anyone paying attention? Perhaps because they made themselves complicit themselves in a racist smear campaign orchestrated to mislead voters and undermine a federal election, and denied themselves the opportunity to reflect on local politics without implicating their own professional interests. There's a reason why the only professional to observe the racism implicit in my character assassination all live outside San Francisco. Who cares? It's not merely the case that Preston helped orchestrated a disinformation campaign that skewed the results of a congressional election, insulated the corrupt leadership of a corporate political party that was , and lied to the public. For what it's worth, Preston was far from alone: other figures who plotted to mislead the public and subvert the integrity of a federal election with included several former campaign staff who had been removed from our campaign after I won the 2020 primary, particularly ; Jackie Thornhill, who was at the time working as an aide to San Francisco Supervisor Raphael Mandelman and on the Board of an LGBTQ Democratic club whose disturbing and has been publicly recognized by several of its recent past presidents; and , the current Chief of Staff to Sheng Thao, the embattled Mayor of Oakland facing a federal . In the time since he smeared me, Preston's district was expanded to include the Tenderloin, one of San Francisco's most diverse neighborhoods. Preston's public racism and white supremacy deserve to be documented, but because writers across San Francisco have unfortunately shared it, they lack the independence to publicly observe it. One journalist--who revealingly chose to remain anonymous--even to the California Globe that he & others published premature articles privileging false claims about me based on nothing more than baseless accusations aimed at subverting an election. [A] lot of us published first without waiting to see who else came forward. Turns out it was no one, and people were hurt in the process, including political campaigns....[M]any journalists were caught up in the [#metoo] movement at the time and believed accusers because so many had gone on for so long without ever being believed. But, as we've seen, it really goes both ways." The various publications that smeared me failed to pursue any modicum of fact checking. Some have by publishing subsequent stories calling into question their previous articles that ultimately insulated corporate control over the Democratic Party by allowing Nancy Pelosi to duck debates despite for one. In fact, it appears that the San Francisco Chronicle 's front-page coverage of played a key role in prompting my character assassination, which followed a week later. Yet none have retracted or corrected any of their stories based on the racist lies that they now acknowledge anonymously. In fact, those stories, ignored evidence, suppressed , mischaracterized their experiences, and led to them being smeared, themselves. Even the Intercept , which once prided itself on bringing the stories of whistleblowers to light, suppressed whistleblowers who tried to exposed the corruption of journalism and politics in San Francisco, and ultimately reinforced it. Writer Akela Lacy initially amplified the racist plot orchestrated by Preston and others, and even after the publication revised its story four times in two months (all without public corrections or retractions), continued to mischaracterize whistleblowers, their roles in the city, their roles on our campaign, and their observations of the orchestration of lies that Lacy published. After one of the whistleblowers faced retaliatory smears, herself, she went on to publish her own reflections in . How is a sitting member of the Board of Supervisors poised to potentially win reelection and represent a minority community in America's "mOsT pRoGrEsSiVe" city without any public discussion of his history of white supremacy? But what about Harris? Anyone familiar with San Francisco politics, the ascent of Kamala Harris, and Nancy Pelosi's role in the Democratic Party, should frankly not be surprised by this history. There are plenty of opportunities for people of color even in racist systems, as long as they support capital and militarism. Some might imagine that, because Harris is herself a person of color from San Francisco currently serving in the White House, the city must not have a problem with race. After all, if the city can send the first female, Black, or Asian Vice President to Washington, how could San Francisco possibly embody racism or white supremacy? They key lies in recalling what racism and white supremacy mean. There are plenty of opportunities for people of color even in racist systems, as long as they support capital and militarism. That is precisely what Harris has done across her entire career. She came to Washington after years working as a predatory prosecutor, embodying domestic militarism. And while she is depicted by journalists as if she were a progressive, Harris has signaled her as part of her presidential campaign. Voices of color who challenge the political orthodoxy that Harris has always embraced endure a remarkably different experience in San Francisco. A proudly "progressive" racist city San Francisco enjoys a reputation as one of the country's most progressive cities, largely because of the cities, cultural legacy, and the relative prominence of LGBTQ voices within the city's political establishment. But the city's racist history looms in the background, and was firmly established long before I was subjected to it. In a previous era, Chinese Americans were with violence, discrimination, and hate. More recently, Latinos have suffered indignities ranging from to gentrification and by fellow San Franciscans. San Francisco's Black communities, meanwhile, have been eviscerated through a combination of aggressive policing and imposed by a brutal housing market. They have also endured one of the most vicious, pernicious, and long-standing examples of environmental racism anywhere in the United States. The Hunters Point shipyard was the site where the Pentagon assembled nuclear bombs ultimately detonated on civilian populations in Japan. But the only weapons of mass destruction in our species' history used intentionally to kill civilians didn't only kill hundreds of thousands of Japanese people . They also tens of thousands of San Franciscans, most of them Black, who have predictably experienced some of the highest rates of breast cancer in the world. In 1964, author and playwright James Baldwin filmed a documentary film exposing the racism in San Francisco that remains widely unobserved. "Take This Hammer" documents a racist history that unfortunately continues unabated to this day. As reviewed by Richard Brody in the New Yorker : Baldwin, guided by the social-services executive Orville Luster, interviews young black residents and learns of the massive uprooting of their neighborhoods under the guise of urban renewal. The movie's participants speak in detail about unemployment, police harassment, despair over the prospects of the civil-rights movement, and anger at their own exclusion from the city's prosperity and governance; one young man discusses his hope for violent revolution by black Americans and his belief that it can be organized. Baldwin, talking with Luster, calls white liberals "missionaries" unwilling to take risks for comprehensive change. How little things change. Smear campaigns , and reporters remain willing to do by indulging lies orchestrated to serve power and enabled by prejudice. Republicans are hardly the only major American political party dedicated to white supremacy. As the voices featured in "Take This Hammer" observe, white supremacy lurks as prominently (even if less visibly) in progressive enclaves as it does in the South. Dean Preston, and the "journalists" across San Francisco who have indulged his self-serving racist lies, offer a walking case study of that unfortunate pattern. subject: Hopeless?

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024]
Friends,
If you’re particularly stressed about the 2024 elections, it can sometimes be easy to start to feel a bit of a sense of hopelessness. People are feeling anxious, and I get it — elections are stressful (for both candidates and voters!), and the stakes are high.
But take it from an optimist: Nothing is a foregone conclusion, and we DO have the power to create the outcomes we all want in this election.
We have an opportunity in just 17 days to protect our Senate majority, take back the House, send Kamala Harris and Tim Walz to the White House, and truly make the kind of progress the American people deserve.
And I’m genuinely optimistic that together, we can get it done! But it won’t happen without a little elbow grease, and it definitely won’t happen if we give in to hopelessness . Are you with me?
Pitch in any amount that’s meaningful to you today, and let’s use these final days to turn out a record-breaking number of Democratic voters. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024]
If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
DONATE $25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024?express_lane=true&amount=25]
DONATE $50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024?express_lane=true&amount=50]
DONATE $100 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024?express_lane=true&amount=100]
OTHER [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024]
At the beginning of last year, I decided to run for re-election to the Senate because I really do have hope for what we can accomplish.
Over the past few years, we’ve proven that with Democrats in power, progress is delivered — from the American Rescue Plan to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to long-overdue progress on gun violence prevention.
I’m a public servant through and through. I love Virginia. I'm proud of what we’ve done so far. And I've got a whole lot more I want to do.
If you’re ready to join me in optimism and in progress, I’m asking you to donate to my re-election campaign right now, so we can reach as many voters as possible before November 5th. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024]
Thank you so much.
-Tim Kaine

_“We pledge to you that we will root out the communists, marxists, fascists and radical left thugs who live like vermin within the confines of our country... The threat from outside forces is far less sinister, dangerous, and grave than the threat from within.”_
**Donald Trump, November 11, 2023**
_“The bigger problem is the enemy from within... We have some very bad people, sick people, radical left lunatics, and I think it should be very easily handled by, if necessary by National Guard, or if really necessary by the Military, because they can’t let that happen.”_
**Donald Trump, October 12, 2024**
When Donald Trump talks about the greatest threats to our nation, he’s not talking about Russia, or Iran. He’s not talking about North Korea testing long range missiles, or an increasingly expansionist China.
He’s talking about you, Peter. He’s talking about the people who would dare to stand up to him at home, in the United States.

This man is a fascist, through and through. We’ve seen his like before. He uses the same rhetoric, sometimes the same exact words and phrases, as men like Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini. And at this point, it’s fair to say that he shares many of their goals.
The last time men like Trump led some of the strongest militaries in the world, more than 65 million people were killed. 420,000 Americans died to stop him and the Axis Powers allied with him.
It does not have to go that far this time. Don’t let the polls convince you this is hopeless. Don’t let the pundits tell you that we’re doomed. We can stop Donald Trump at the ballot box, and we’ve got the tools we need to do it.

He’s not talking about North Korea testing long range missiles, or an increasingly expansionist China. He’s talking about you, Peter. He’s talking about the people who would dare to stand up to him at home, in the United States. “The threat from within” is us. This man is a fascist, through and through. We’ve seen his like before. He uses the same rhetoric, sometimes the same exact words and phrases, as men like Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini. And at this point, it’s fair to say that he shares many of their goals. The last time men like Trump led some of the strongest militaries in the world, more than 65 million people were killed. 420,000 Americans died to stop him and the Axis Powers allied with him. It does not have to go that far this time. Don’t let the polls convince you this is hopeless. Don’t let the pundits tell you that we’re doomed. We can stop Donald Trump at the ballot box, and we’ve got the tools we need to do it. All we need is a final push these next three weeks. And to get the job done, we need you with us. It’s no accident that Cooke is the frontrunner for regular folks.”_
And he emphasized what we’re doing on the campaign trail is historic:
_“I have observed and participated in multiple Wisconsin Democratic U.S. House campaigns. Cooke is connecting to voters throughout the 3rd CD and generating a positive enthusiasm and outpouring of strong support. She has no meaningful rival in fundraising and organizing in the 3rd CD. I've got my friendship bracelet on as I write this out to you, friend — and I'm fully in my "Florida!!!" era.
That's right, even if my kids say I'm too old to be one, I'm a Swiftie! I love Taylor Swift, and I'm so excited she's here in Miami this weekend for the final leg of the Eras Tour.
While I'm a little too busy on the campaign trail to sneak away for the concert, I hope Taylor will treat Floridians to the song she and Florence Welch wrote about our beautiful state.**In fact, I'm so enamored with our state that I have my own "Love Story" to Florida. It has a lot to do with why I'm running to defeat Rick Scott and give our people the leadership they deserve in the U.S. Senate. **
**Can I share that love story with you, friend?[(Before you continue, I've also got to ask you to chip in $5 or more to my campaign to defeat Rick Scott — because polls show us tied with just 17 days until Election Day!) ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95389962/506562975/1820369458?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk2303-fr-nd&recurring=1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS8xMDc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzg1ZWVkZTktNTg4ZS1lZjExLTg0NzQtMDAwZDNhOThmYTZiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CAd4ikbLbL0n_dcTtfBRIzqL_tG3LNWEyqQRvZpCagg=)**
Here's what I remember the first time I stepped outside of the airport here in Florida to visit my sister: the welcoming warmth of the weather, the beautiful greenery all around, and the lively, diverse communities who were just as welcoming as the heat that enveloped us.
**It didn't even take 10 minutes to know "All Too Well" that the Sunshine State would be my eventual home.**
I was right. I fell in love in Florida (love ya, Robert 🩷), raised a family of my own here, and began dedicating my career to serving this state. I worked to protect what makes me love Florida so much: our beautiful wildlife and coral reefs. On top of that, I led new programs to improve access to affordable health care for Floridians.
**"Call It What You Want," but this immigrant from Ecuador became a Florida girl at heart, and I eventually had the incredible privilege of serving my community in the U.S. House of Representatives, becoming the first South American immigrant in Congress.**
In the House:
* I wrote the bill to expand seniors' Medicare Advantage coverage to ensure more Americans could get the care they deserve.
* I worked with Republicans to provide economic relief to families and small businesses.
* I secured $200 million for Everglades restoration.
* I fought tirelessly for common sense gun safety reforms and served as the vice chair of the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.

So "long story short," friend, I truly love Florida. I will do whatever I can to better our state and the people who live here. My opponent, Rick Scott, on the other hand — talk about "The Smallest Man Who Ever Lived." He's looking out for only two people: himself and Donald Trump. He's done absolutely nothing to help the people of this state, and yet he's spending his fraudulently earned, multimillion-dollar fortune to cling to power.
**I'm ready for the day when we can say this about Rick Scott: "I Forgot That You Existed." **We are so close to defeating him and making that Taylor Swift song a reality: Polls show us TIED, and the experts at Inside Elections have increased my chances of winning!

**But that doesn't change the fact that I'm up against the $37 million that Rick Scott is shelling out in ads to defeat me, and I still haven't closed in on my $500,000 daily fundraising goal.[So if you're "...Ready For It?" — ready to win this election — then I'm asking you to rush a donation of $5, or whatever you can, to help me win in Florida and protect our Democratic Senate majority!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95389963/506562976/1820369458?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk2303-fr-nd&recurring=1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS8xMDc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzg1ZWVkZTktNTg4ZS1lZjExLTg0NzQtMDAwZDNhOThmYTZiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CAd4ikbLbL0n_dcTtfBRIzqL_tG3LNWEyqQRvZpCagg=)**

#
Friend of Life,

Did you know that America's most popular diaper brands, including Huggies, Pampers, Hello Bello, and Honest Co., all support abortion?

This is peak irony. Brands that provide a necessity for babies also financially and/or publicly support an act that intentionally kills innocent children in the womb.

As pro-life people, we can do something to put a stop to this.

**Live Action is hosting a diaper drive with EveryLife -- the first pro-life diaper company -- to help mothers and their babies in need.**

If you're tired of supporting brands that don't align with your pro-life values, you can do something now to help women AND support a pro-life business.

**Your gift of just $50 will provide six packs of EveryLife diapers to a mom who is considering abortion or is facing a crisis and help her embrace life. Our goal is to provide 34 boxes of diapers to every state.**
